title: Psalm 110: The King Who Is Also a Priest
summary: In a solemn oracle the LORD speaks to the psalmist's lord, the king, inviting him to sit at God's right hand until his enemies become his footstool, and sends his scepter out from Zion. God then swears an oath that this king is a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek. The psalm ends on the day of wrath, with the Lord at the king's right hand crushing kings, and the king drinking from a brook by the road and lifting up his head.

from.where: The Study Bible's introduction to the Psalms
from.text: Royal psalms are about the king of Israel: his crowning, his wedding, his battles, God's promise to his family (Psalms 2, 18, 20, 21, 45, 72, 89, 101, 110, 132, 144).

line: The LORD invites the king to sit at his right hand and swears that he is a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek; it is the Old Testament text the New Testament quotes most often about Christ.
guide: Ask whether your picture of Jesus has grown small: a teacher, a helper, but not Lord. Christians live in the until of verse 1, when not everything is put right yet. If you find it hard to pray, verse 4 says there is someone who prays for you, whose priesthood does not end.

stanzas.title: First oracle: sit at my right hand
The scepter from Zion and a willing people
Second oracle: a priest forever like Melchizedek
The day of wrath and the king's triumph

verses.t: A Psalm of David. The LORD said to my Lord: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.”
The LORD extends Your mighty scepter from Zion: “Rule in the midst of Your enemies.”
Your people shall be willing on Your day of battle. Arrayed in holy splendor, from the womb of the dawn, to You belongs the dew of Your youth.
The LORD has sworn and will not change His mind: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
The Lord is at Your right hand; He will crush kings in the day of His wrath.
He will judge the nations, heaping up the dead; He will crush the leaders far and wide.
He will drink from the brook by the road; therefore He will lift up His head.
